summary:
There is no standalone "i1410" in Richard Cornwell's sims repo; the 1410 lives inside the I7000 family as the i7010 simulator (I7000/i7010_cpu.c, i7010_chan.c, i7010_sys.c, i7010_defs.h, plus shared i7000_cdr.c/cdp/lpr/con/mt/dsk/chan). The CPU unit has `set CPU 1401` (MODEL 1, "Emulate a 1401") and `set CPU 7010` ("sets IBM 1410/7010 emulation"); there is no separate 1410-vs-7010 model flag, so it is really a 7010 with 1401 mode, and 1410 behaviour is the subset (2 channels, 80K). Each source file carries an MIT-style permission notice (Cornwell copyright, 2006); the repo has no top-level LICENSE detected by GitHub. It ships a real regression test: I7000/tests/i7010_test.ini boots tests/i7010/diag.bin (2,930,826 bytes, byte-identical in size to sky-visions.com/ibm/7010/d90_1410.bin, the recovered 1410/7010 diagnostic tape) and drives it with `expect "OPTION?"` sending C0 (CPU), CU, T0 (tape), W0, and ST02 (card deck st02.txt in SimH ~raw format). STATUS.txt says: protection mode has errors, T020 tape diags fail, "PR108 not tested". Cornwell's sky-visions site hosts the 1410 software corpus: PR-155 master tape (pr155_mst.bcd, 4.1 MB), a pre-generated PR-155 system tape sof.tp, PR-108 tape (pr108.bcd, 4.6 MB) with Autocoder/IOCS/Fortran/COBOL/RPG, sample .job decks (a.job Autocoder, c.job COBOL, f.job Fortran hello world, f108.job primes, pi.job, prime.job, laplace.job), .ini scripts for SimH, and d90_1410.bin diagnostics. This is the best cross-check oracle: run the same tape/deck under SimH i7010 and diff printer output (SimH lp attach to a text file).

Jay Jaeger (github cube1us) has three relevant repos. (a) cube1us/1410: a cycle-level 1410 simulator in Borland C++ Builder/VCL (Windows only), GPL-3.0 (COPYING + Copyright.txt, 1998-2000, 2019), with units for 1415 console (UI1415L/IO/CE), 1402 reader/punch, 1403 printer, 729 tape, channels, and a Core/ directory of .cor core images (cc01.cor 40,005 bytes; ilentest.cor, ilentst2.cor, insttest.cor 320,005 bytes each — instruction-length and index-register hand tests described in note1410.txt, plus cc01 = the CC01 limited CPU instruction test). Repo still active (updated 2026-08-08). Not easily runnable on macOS/Linux, but the C++ instruction implementations and the 1415 console fonts (fontlib) are readable reference. (b) cube1us/IBM1410FPGA: VHDL generated from the 1410/1415 ALDs (10,596 logic blocks, 14,021 signals), ~1000+ files under VHDL/ (ALD_*.vhdl with _tb testbenches), no LICENSE file on GitHub; the companion IBM1410SMS (C#, ALD database tool) is GPL-3.0 and IBM1410Console (C#, lights/switches/console/I-O for the FPGA) has no license file. Per his site (mid-2026) the FPGA passes CPU diagnostics CU01 (1410 mode) and M011A (1401 compatibility mode), runs I/O diagnostics, boots PR-108 and full PR-155 including sysgen, with tape over UDP and 1414 unit-record I/O. It is the most faithful reference in existence for cycle-level questions, but as a diff oracle it needs hardware (Digilent Nexys 4).

Browser/JavaScript 1401 or 1410 emulators: none found. Searches (web + GitHub API for "1401 ibm language:javascript/typescript") turned up only aarjavchauhan/IBM1401_generative (JS, not an emulator) and PCjs (no 1401/1410 machine). Existing 1401 emulators are SimH I1401 (C, Supnik, MIT-style, i1401_cpu/cd/lp/mt/dp/iq/sys; simh.trailing-edge.com kits ceo1401.zip diagnostics+SPS, 1401_fortran_autocoder.tgz, 1401koans.zip), ROPE (Java IDE, GPL-2.0, wraps Van Snyder's Fortran-90 Autocoder and SimH), Swift (sanzaru/ibm-1401, incomplete), C++ (ApoorvaJ, incomplete), BAL360 (moshix), Rob Storey's Windows emulator, and the Unreal "VDC" 3D datacenter. The 1401-side test corpus (ibm-1401.info, GitHub org IBM-1401: autocoder, disasm, Fortran-II, dump) is useful for the 1410's 1401-compatibility mode only with care: Van Snyder's code chart notes that 1410 does not interpret 1401 op codes #, H, P, Q, Y or 1-9, that G/J/R are 1410-only ops, and that on the 1410 M and L are I/O only — i.e. native 1401 object decks are NOT binary-compatible with native 1410 mode; they only make sense with the 1401-compat switch, which SimH i7010 models (`set CPU 1401`, op_1401[] table, instruction translation at i7010_cpu.c ~line 941-999). The real diagnostic for that mode is IBM's M014B "1410/7010 1401 Compatibility" test (bitsavers /pdf/ibm/1410/diagnostics/DIAGV100/, 5.6 MB PDF listing).

Reference material: bitsavers /pdf/ibm/1410/ has the Principles of Operation (A22-0526, -2, -3, May63), A22-1407-2 reference, the Oct-61 CE manual, 1414 I/O synchronizer OEM info (A22-6701), Autocoder manuals (C28-0309, C28-0326), and a diagnostics/ tree (DIAGV100..DIAGV601) with scanned listings incl. CC01A limited CPU test, TC50C tape diagnostic control program, M014B 1401 compat, and an Introduction to Diagnostics. bitsavers /bits/IBM/1410/ has only 1410-PR-108/ (jpr108-2024.bcd 1.3 MB, jpr108-2024.zip 308 KB, four photos; direct curl of the zip returns 403, needs a browser/referrer). Ken Shirriff's posts give visual/physical facts (1401 core: 4,000 chars base, 14 planes 50x80, 8 bits per location = 6 BCD + word mark + parity, 11.5 us cycle; 1403: 132 columns, chain of 48 chars x5, 600 lpm, hammers, 11.1 us/0.001 in chain step; boot/word-mark/card code explanation) — all 1401-specific, but the 1402/1403/729 peripherals and card/BCD codes are shared with the 1410. Van Snyder's "IBM 1401/1440/1460/1410/7010 Character Code Chart" (ibm-1401.info/Van1401-CodeChart.pdf, 2 pages) is the single best card-code/BCD/ASCII mapping table, including SimH and Pierce ASCII conventions and the 1410-specific notes.

facts.claim: Cornwell's sims repo has no I1410 directory; the 1410 is emulated by the i7010 simulator under I7000/ (files i7010_cpu.c, i7010_chan.c, i7010_defs.h, i7010_sys.c plus shared i7000_cdr.c, i7000_cdp.c, i7000_lpr.c, i7000_con.c, i7000_mt.c, i7000_dsk.c, i7000_chan.c, i7000_com.c, i7000_chron.c, i7000_ht.c).

i7010_cpu.c help text: 'The CPU can be set to a IBM 1401 or IBM 1410/7010'; `set CPU 1401` = 1401 emulation (MODEL(1)), `set CPU 7010` = 1410/7010 emulation (MODEL(2)); options prot, float, pri; there is no distinct 1410 model setting.

i7010_cpu.c has a 1401 opcode table op_1401[64] and translates 1401 instructions to 1410 form in 1401 mode (comments 'Handle 1401 emulation mode', 'Translate instruction from 1401 to 1410', 'Handle 1401 I/O opcodes').
Cornwell i7010 source files carry an MIT-style permission notice, Copyright (c) 2006 Richard Cornwell; GitHub reports no top-level license for rcornwell/sims.

rcornwell/sims ships I7000/tests/i7010_test.ini which boots tests/i7010/diag.bin (2,930,826 bytes) on mta0 with `set cpu 80k prot float pri`, answers the diagnostic monitor prompt 'OPTION?' with C0, CU, T0, W0 and ST02, attaches the printer to diag.lst, and feeds card deck st02.txt (SimH ~raw format, 494,247 bytes) to cdr0.
The test diag.bin is the same size (2,930,826 bytes) as sky-visions.com/ibm/7010/d90_1410.bin, described there as 'Diagnostics for the 1410 and 7010 and most of the peripherals'.
Cornwell's STATUS.txt for i7010: 'Protection mode has some errors left', 'T020 tape diags fail', 'Disks may work', 'PR108 not tested'.
i7010_sys.c device table includes cpu, chan, cdr, cdp, stack, lpr, con, mta/mtb/mtc tape, hsdrm/drm drums, dsk, coml/com, chron.

sky-visions.com hosts 1410/7010 software: PR-155 (7010/pr155/pr155_mst.bcd 4,105,577 bytes, sof.tp, gensgf.job/.ini, gensof.job/.ini, autotest.job, pi.job, prime.job, laplace.job, pr155.ini), PR-108 (7010/pr108/pr108.bcd 4,616,734 bytes, pr108_20k.tp, a.job, c.job, f.job, f108.job, s.job, s20k.job, a.ini), and diagnostics (7010/d90_1410.bin, d90_1410.ini).
sky-visions says the PR-155 master tape comes from Paul Pierce's tape adc00036 with parity errors fixed; the site lacks a disk master tape.
cube1us/1410 is a cycle-level IBM 1410 simulator in C++ (Borland C++ Builder + VCL, Windows), licensed GPL-3.0, copyright 1998-2000, 2019 Jay R. Jaeger; last updated 2026-08-08.

cube1us/1410 contains units for 1415 console (UI1415L, UI1415IO, UI1415CE), 1402 reader/punch/stacker (UI1402*), 1403 printer (UI1403, UIPRINTER), 729 tape (UI729TAPE, UITAPETAU, UITAPEUNIT), channel, arithmetic, branch, edit/data, debug window, power panel, and a BCD table (ubcd.cpp/.txt), plus fontlib with 1415 console and 1403 printer fonts (.FON/.FNT).

cube1us/1410/Core holds test core images: cc01.cor (40,005 bytes), ilentest.cor, ilentst2.cor, insttest.cor (320,005 bytes each). note1410.txt documents ilentst as instruction-length decode tests at addresses 00100-02100 (one per opcode A S ? ! M % D Z E C T J X R B W V G , lozenge / . and I/O ops) and index-register tests at 02200-02288 using all 15 index registers at 00025+.
cube1us/1410 README TODO: no disk support (130x/1311); PR-155 OS cannot reside on a 1311.

cube1us/IBM1410FPGA is a VHDL implementation of the 1410 generated from the ALDs (directories VHDL/ and dbModel/, >1000 files in VHDL/ named ALD_<sheet>_*.vhdl with *_tb.vhdl testbenches); GitHub detects no license file; last updated 2026-08-21.
cube1us/IBM1410SMS (C#, ALD capture database) is GPL-3.0; cube1us/IBM1410Console (C#, lights/switches/console/I-O for the FPGA) has no license file detected.

Jaeger's FPGA status page: CPU diagnostics CU01 (1410 mode) and M011A (1401 mode) pass; I/O diagnostics run; boots PR-108 and full PR-155 including Autocoder and PR-155 sysgen; tape via UDP with PC-side support (late 2025); 1414 unit-record I/O (mid-2026); board is Digilent Nexys 4.
The 1410's 1401 compatibility mode was a hardwired (not microcoded) feature enabled by a console switch.

No JavaScript/TypeScript/WebAssembly browser emulator of the IBM 1401 or 1410 was found; GitHub searches for '1401 ibm language:javascript' return only aarjavchauhan/IBM1401_generative (not an emulator) and for language:typescript nothing; PCjs has no 1401/1410 machine.

Other 1401 emulators: SimH I1401 (C, Robert Supnik, MIT-style notice, files i1401_cpu.c, i1401_cd.c, i1401_lp.c, i1401_mt.c, i1401_dp.c, i1401_iq.c, i1401_sys.c, i1401_defs.h, i1401_dat.h; simulates 1402, 1403, 1311, 729, inquiry); sanzaru/ibm-1401 (Swift, incomplete); ApoorvaJ/IBM-1401 (C++, incomplete); moshix/IBM1401 (S/360 BAL for MVS 3.8); Rob Storey Windows emulator (2002); Unreal 'VDC' 3D datacenter (Mac).

SimH 'Classic' software kits for the 1401: ceo1401.zip (diagnostics + SPS assembler; bootable diagnostics tape circa 1962), 1401_fortran_autocoder.tgz (courtesy Van Snyder), 1401koans.zip (three single-card programs). No 1410 kits there.

ROPE (Ron's Own Programming Environment) is a Java IDE for the 1401, GPL-2.0, wrapping Van Snyder's Fortran-90 Autocoder (v3.13) and SimH; current source github.com/lucaseverini/ROPE (Luca Severini), older github.com/jpf/ROPE; includes sample lincoln.s. Autocoder binaries are 32-bit (macOS/Windows compatibility issues).

ibm-1401.info resources: Van1401-CodeChart.pdf ('IBM 1401/1440/1460/1410/7010 Character Code Chart', BCD order and collating order, with print glyph, three ASCII conventions (SimH, Pierce primary, Pierce alternative), op code, card punch code, BCD bits), 1401-CardDeckFormats.html (three object-deck loader styles; word-separator char sets word mark on next char), 1403-CarriageControl.html, sample programs (99 bottles, Mandelbrot, Bitcoin, Hexapawn), Van Snyder utilities, 1401-FORTRAN-SIMH.html.

Van Snyder code chart 1410-specific notes: 'D, T and X have different meanings in 1401, 1460 and 1410. 1410 does not interpret #, H, P, Q, Y or 1-9. G, J and R are 1410 only. M and L on 1410 are only for I/O.' '% and @ are standard on 1410. 7010 and 1410 are compatible.' Card code 2-8 prints as cent sign on 1410. Word Separator = CA841 (0-5-8), Record Mark = A82 (0-2-8), Group Mark = CBA8421 (12-7-8).
ibm-1401.info '1401 REPAIR QUIZ' (1401-test-0001.html) is a technician study quiz, not a diagnostic program.

GitHub org IBM-1401 hosts autocoder (Fortran), disasm (Fortran), autocoder_1401 (the real Autocoder in 1401 assembly), Fortran-v3m0/v3m4 sources, dump, tpdump (SimH tape dumper), 3to5/5to3 address converters; lkesteloot/1401 has 1401 programs in C.

bitsavers /pdf/ibm/1410/ includes A22-0526-2, -3, A22-0526 and May63 1410 Principles of Operation, A22-1407-2 1410 reference (Nov61), 1410_CE_Manual_Oct61, 223-2589 System Fundamentals (Nov63), A22-6701 1414 I/O Synchronizer OEM information, A22-0530-1 priority feature, C28-0309(-1) Autocoder, C28-0326-1/-2 OS Autocoder, IOCS, COBOL, Fortran, sysgen, sort, utility manuals, and subdirs CE_Instruction_Reference_Maintenance/, diagnostics/, drawings/.

bitsavers /pdf/ibm/1410/diagnostics/ has DIAGV100, V200, V201, V202-K2, V300, V301, V400, V500, V500-K2, V600, V601, V601-K2; DIAGV100 contains 1410_7010_Diagnostics_Summary_Pages.pdf, 1410_7010_Introduction_to_Diagnostics.pdf, CC01A_1410_Limited_CPU_Instruction_Test.pdf, m003e_1410_Program_Addressable_Clock_Test.pdf, M014B_1410_7010_1401_Compatibility.pdf (5,642,919 bytes), TC50C_1410_7010_Diagnostic_Tape_Control_Program.pdf, listings.pdf.

bitsavers /bits/IBM/1410/ has only 1410-PR-108/ containing jpr108-2024.bcd (1.3 MB), jpr108-2024.zip (308 KB) and four JPGs (1410_1..4.jpg), dated 2024-03-24; a plain curl of the zip returns HTTP 403.

Ken Shirriff 1401 core memory post: 4,000 characters base (expandable to 16K), 14 core planes each 50x80, 8 bits per location (6 BCD + word mark + parity), X select/inhibit and Y select/sense wires, 5x10 X and 8x10 Y matrix switches, memory cycle 11.5 us, 6 sparse I/O planes of 297 cores for brush/hammer checks. (1401 facts; 1410 differs.)

Ken Shirriff 1403 posts: chain of 48 characters repeated 5 times, 132 hammers each with an electromagnet, chain moves 0.001 inch every 11.1 us giving a vernier alignment so only one hammer lines up at a time, 600 lpm on 1403 (10 lines/s), 100/120/132-column widths at 10 cpi, 14 7/8 x 11 in green-bar paper; interactive print-chain animation at static.righto.com/ibm1401/printchain.html.

Ken Shirriff 1401 boot post: Load button reads first card into 1-80, sets word mark at 1 and executes; bootstrap cards set word marks and clear storage; program cards carry code left and loader instructions right; word marks cannot be punched on cards so loaders set them with Set Word Mark (',') instructions; Clear Storage is '/'. (1401 facts; 1410 load path differs.)

Other Shirriff 1401 posts: germanium transistor/SMS logic (2021/03), Christmas card (2017/12), line printer music (2019/09), Mandelbrot (2015/03), 'The printer that wouldn't print' (2018/09); label index at righto.com/search/label/ibm1401. shirriff/groupmark repo proposes Unicode group mark.

tables: 1410-relevant BCD/card codes for control characters (from Van Snyder chart)
open_questions: Exact license of cube1us/IBM1410FPGA and IBM1410Console (no LICENSE file detected; author's site does not state one) — ask Jay Jaeger before reusing VHDL-derived tables.

Whether Cornwell's i7010 in '7010' mode can be constrained to a strict 1410 configuration (2 channels, 80K, no float) for diffing — the CPU has MEMAMOUNT/OPTION flags but no separate 1410 model; needs a read of i7010_defs.h/channel code.
Which diagnostics on d90_1410.bin correspond to bitsavers listings (CC01A, M014B, TC50C) and which fail under SimH (T020C per STATUS/test.ini) — needs running the test.ini locally.
Contents of bitsavers jpr108-2024.zip (403 to curl; likely readable with browser) and how it differs from sky-visions pr108.bcd.
No 1410-mode 1415 console character set / print behaviour was verified from a primary source here — read A22-0526 PrincOps console chapter for that.
1403 chain character set on the 1410 (A chain vs H chain; the 1410 also supported 1403 model 2/3) — verify in 1410 PrincOps or the 1403 component description, not covered in this pass.

verdict.topic: IBM 1410 emulators / simulators / test software survey — adversarial check

refuted.claim: cube1us/1410 note1410.txt instruction-length tests cover 'one per opcode A S ? ! M % D Z E C T J X R B W V G , lozenge / .' — with M listed as the Multiply op (summary text and Core/.cor claim).
refuted.why: Jaeger's note1410.txt does label 00500 as 'Multiply Instruction (M)', but that is a slip in his notes. In the 1410 Principles of Operation the Multiply op code is @ and Divide is % (A22-0526-3 text: 'Multiply M a,b @ (A) (B)' in the instruction summary; instruction format 'M @ aaaaa bbbbb'). On the 1410, op code M is the tape/unit-record I/O op (Move mode) — Van Snyder's chart says the same ('M and L on 1410 are only for I/O'). An emulator that decoded M as Multiply would be applying the 1401 op code (1401 Multiply = M) to the 1410.
refuted.correction: 1410 native op codes: Multiply = @, Divide = %; M and L are I/O (move-mode / load-mode data transfer). note1410.txt's '(M)' for Multiply is the author's shorthand error, not a 1410 fact. Also 02100 lists I/O ops 'M, L, U, K, F, 4, 2'.
refuted.source: http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_PrincOps.pdf (instruction summary; local text extract princops_a22-0526-3.txt lines 2062, 11434, 11844); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cube1us/1410/master/note1410.txt lines 17-38

refuted.claim: Table '1410-relevant BCD/card codes': Tape Segment (") = 0-7-8, BCD bits CA8421.
refuted.why: The Van Snyder chart row reads 'Tape Segment 0-7-8 A8421' (no C bit). A8421 has 4 bits set, so with even parity (C = even) on 7-track BCD tape the C bit is absent; the finder added a C. The Group Mark row (12-7-8, CBA8421) is correct.
refuted.correction: Tape Segment: card 0-7-8, BCD A8421 (no check bit). Group Mark: 12-7-8, CBA8421. Record Mark: 0-2-8, A82. Word Separator: 0-5-8, CA841. Mode Change: 11-7-8, B8421.

refuted.claim: cube1us/1410 and companion repos: 'the FPGA ... per his site' — status page gives no license; the FPGA repo license is unknown.
refuted.why: Minor, but the finder's open question can be narrowed: the computercollection.net FPGA status page states the application source is GPL-licensed ('GPL'). GitHub still detects no LICENSE file in cube1us/IBM1410FPGA (api: license null, contents only VHDL/ and dbModel/), so the author's intent is GPL even though the repo has no license file.
refuted.correction: Author's site says GPL; repo lacks a LICENSE file. Still worth confirming with Jaeger before deriving tables, but the intent is documented.

upgraded.claim: Jaeger's FPGA status: CU01 (1410 mode) and M011A (1401 mode) pass (early Aug 2023); as of mid-2026 passes 1410 and 1401 I/O diagnostics, runs PR-108 and full PR-155 including Autocoder/compilers and PR-155 sysgen; tape via 1414 TAU logic in FPGA + PC-side program over UDP (late 2025); blog #42 'IBM 1414 Unit Record I/O Synchronizer' dated 2026-08-21; board is Digilent Nexys 4 ('might have even fit on a Nexys 2').

The 1410's 1401 compatibility mode is selected by a console switch (not microcode): PrincOps 'Compatibility Switch (Figure 56), when at the 1401 setting, makes it possible to run IBM 1401 programs on the 1410. Ordinarily, the switch should be in the 1410 setting.' The 1401 COMPAT light shows the mode; index lists 'Compatibility Switch, 1415 Test Panel'. Jaeger's page states it was 'all done in hard wired logic'.
upgraded.source: http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_PrincOps.pdf (1415 Console chapter, 'Compatibility Controls'; local extract lines 6630-6640, 6864-6870, 12107) ; https://www.computercollection.net/index.php/the-ibm-1410-data-processing-system/

upgraded.claim: sky-visions: PR-155 master tape derives from Paul Pierce's tape adc00036 with parity errors cleaned up; site has no disk master tape so no disk-resident PR-155 can be generated.
upgraded.source: https://sky-visions.com/ibm/ibm7010_soft.shtml (fetched HTML: 'Pierces site tape adc00036, but I fixed it to clean up some parity errors in the data'; 'disk master tape so we can't at the moment generate a disk')

upgraded.claim: Cornwell i7010: help text 'The CPU can be set to a IBM 1401 or IBM 1410/7010'; MODEL(1) '1401' = 'Emulate a 1401', MODEL(2) '7010' = 'Emulate a 7010'; memory settable 10K..100K in 10K steps (MAXMEMSIZE 100000 in i7000_defs.h); default unit MODEL(2)|MEMAMOUNT(9)|OPTION_PRIO|OPTION_FLOAT. No 1410-specific model; 1401-mode translation code at i7010_cpu.c ~941-1000 maps 1401 M/L/D/P/Y to OP_MOV with modifiers and 1401 K/F to channel control.

STATUS.txt i7010 entry (verbatim): 'Protection mode has some errors left. Protection mode does not handle setting H or L to 0. T020 tape diags fail. Disks may work. PR108 not tested.' i7010_test.ini echoes 'CU26 not working yet' and 'Expect error 17 on T020C test'.
No browser/JavaScript IBM 1401 or 1410 emulator exists in public search results (PCjs has none; retrocomputingforum thread lists only SimH, ROPE, BAL360, Windows/Swift/C++ ports).
upgraded.source: WebSearch 'IBM 1401 emulator JavaScript browser online' — https://www.pcjs.org/ ; https://retrocomputingforum.com/t/ibm-1401-emulators/3143 ; https://github.com/moshix/IBM1401

additions.claim: 1410 storage: five 1411 models — 10,000 / 20,000 / 40,000 / 60,000 / 80,000 positions (models 1-5, 'A' suffix adds an E frame). Data Channel 2 is a special feature (channel 1 standard); 1410 max is 2 channels, 7010 has 4 and addresses 100K. For diffing against Cornwell's i7010, set memory to 80K or less and expect a 7010-default config (PRIO+FLOAT on) unless you 'set cpu nofloat nopri'.

In 1401 mode a 10K 1410 behaves as an 8K 1401; every larger 1410 behaves as a 16K 1401. 1401 features usable in 1401 mode: additional storage, multiply-divide, expanded print edit, advanced programming (indexing, SAR, move record), print storage, high-low-equal compare, read-punch release, sense switches. NOT supported in 1401 mode: column binary, compressed tape, punch-feed read, serial I/O adapter (1009/1011/1012/1412/1418/1419), process overlap, selective tape listing, space suppression.

Behavioural differences in 1401 mode that a 1410 emulator must model differently from a true 1401: (1) input characters with bad parity — the 1401 forces them valid by flipping C; the 1410 stores an asterisk (*) instead; (2) divide with an initially blank B field and zero quotient — 1401 leaves blanks, 1410-in-1401-mode converts them to zeros; (3) 1401-mode I/O errors are governed by the console I/O Check Stop switch and 1401 I/O Check-Reset switch, which are inoperative in 1410 mode.
additions.source: http://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_PrincOps.pdf ('Differences in 1401 and 1410 system operation', 'Compatibility Controls'; local extract lines 6871-6885, 11011-11025)

additions.claim: Cornwell's 1401-mode translation (i7010_cpu.c) maps 1401 op codes to 1410 internal ops: B with various lengths -> OP_BCE or OP_B; U/W/V keep modifier; K/F issued as immediate channel control commands then become NOP; M/L without X-control become OP_MOV with modifier C / X; D -> OP_MOV mod '1'; P -> OP_MOV mod '.'; Y -> OP_MOV mod '2'; 1401 I/O digits 1-7 handled as 'Handle 1401 I/O opcodes'. This is a useful reference for how a 1401-mode decoder can reuse the 1410 Move engine.

The Van Snyder chart's 1410-specific print glyph column: on the 1410 the 2-8 card code (BCD 'A' alone) prints as ¢, and 0-7 (CA421) is the 1410 '*' op-code marker; 12-7 (BA421) is 'S?R' flagged 1410 (Store A-address? register); 0-3 T is marked 1460/1410. These ¶ marks are the finder's basis and are read correctly.

verdict.notes: Checked with primary sources downloaded to the scratchpad (i7010_cpu.c, i7010_defs.h, i7000_defs.h, STATUS.txt, i7010_test.ini, note1410.txt, Van1401-CodeChart.pdf, sky-visions HTML, and the A22-0526-3 1410 PrincOps text extract already present in the scratchpad). Not re-verified: byte sizes of diag.bin/d90_1410.bin/pr155_mst.bcd/pr108.bcd (finder's HEAD requests; not load-bearing), the SimH Classic kit list, ROPE details, the 1401-only Shirriff facts (out of scope for 1410 behaviour), and bitsavers directory listings. The 1401-vs-1410 confusion found: the summary's opcode letter list treats M as 1410 Multiply (it is @ on the 1410; M is I/O) — inherited from a slip in Jaeger's note1410.txt. The finder's own 1410/1401 op-code caveats (from Van Snyder) are otherwise consistent with the 1410 PrincOps. Cornwell's help text for MODEL(2) says 'Emulate a 7010' in the MTAB but 'sets IBM 1410/7010 emulation' in cpu_help — the finder's quote is accurate. Group Mark = CBA8421 and ¢ = 2-8 confirmed; only Tape Segment bits were wrong.
